children.title: Shortcuts: the `[shortcuts]` table, its validator and the effective map, engine-only
children.body:
## Parent

Child of #44 (Shortcuts and windows), first of three. The registry and its off-limits and reserved lists are `quill_engine::commands` (#119); the settings file is `quill-engine::settings` (#50, ADR 0010; 26 KB with five submodules, `file`, `reading`, `state`, `writing`, `xdg`); the rules are `docs/shortcuts.md` and ADR 0011; the engine may not see `gtk` by ADR 0008.

## What to build

The `[shortcuts]` table read, validated and overlaid on the defaults, in the engine. After this ticket `Settings::shortcuts()` returns the effective map — every Command with the chords it should have — and a list of refusals, each with its line and its reason; nothing in the app reads it yet (next ticket).

Decided details:

- **Format**: `[shortcuts]` keys are Command ids as quoted strings, values are arrays of chords in GTK accelerator syntax (`<Control><Shift>k`, `F9`); the first chord is the labelled one.
- **Parsing**, narrowing #44 § Format ("`gtk::accelerator_parse` decides what parses"): the engine parses only the shape — `<Modifier>` groups then one non-empty key token — and refuses from that; an unknown key name is refused by the app's `gtk::accelerator_parse` at install (#124), through the same refusal list, so the engine never carries GDK's key-name table.
- **Refusals**, one reason string each: unknown id; chord of the wrong shape; off-limits or reserved chord (the registry's lists); any chord with `<Super>`, or with both `<Control>` and `<Alt>`; a chord already installed earlier in the file (first entry keeps it). A refused entry leaves that Command's defaults untouched; the other entries still apply.
- **Overlay**: the defaults are immutable in the registry; `effective(defaults, accepted) -> BTreeMap<CommandId, Vec<Chord>>` is computed on every read, so removing an entry restores the default and `[]` unbinds.
- `--settings <path>` redirects both reads and writes of `settings.toml` to `<path>` for that launch; the rule that a flag launch writes nothing (`docs/architecture.md` § Command-line flags) applies to the XDG file only. Parsed in `quill/src/flags.rs` and documented in § Command-line flags in this ticket — #120 edits the same two places in parallel; expect a one-line merge.
- Unknown keys and tables in the file are kept, as ADR 0010 requires; `[shortcuts]` follows the same reading and writing modules the other keys use.

Pieces: none.

**Size**: about 45 tool calls by the rubric — one engine module deepened (read `reading.rs` and `writing.rs` by range), one flag, no Gate run. The landed shape is #79 (61 calls, 93k peak) to #102 (127, 169k).

**Reading**: #44 § Solution and § Implementation Decisions (Format, Rules, Apply), with the parsing narrowing above. `docs/shortcuts.md` § Reserved chords, § Off-limits chords, § Rebinding. ADR 0010, ADR 0011 § Consequences. `docs/architecture.md` § Settings and § Command-line flags. `legacy/app/js/core.js` `buildKeymap` only, for first-wins. Skip `quill/src/chrome.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A fixture with every refusal kind and every accepted kind (replace, add a second chord, unbind with `[]`, give a chord-less Command one) is checked entry by entry: the outcome, the reason string, and the effective chords.
- [ ] Removing an entry between two reads restores the default; a duplicate chord later in the file is refused and the earlier keeps it.
- [ ] Every chord in `docs/shortcuts.md` passes the engine's shape parser (an engine test); `gtk::accelerator_parse` accepts every one of them too (a `quill` test, since the engine may not call GTK).
- [ ] `--settings <path>` is honoured for reads and writes and documented; a launch with it touches no XDG file.
- [ ] `tools/gate check` green.

## Blocked by

- #119

children.title: Shortcuts: the settings watch with `notify`, every setting applied live, refusals logged once
children.body:
## Parent

Child of #44 (Shortcuts and windows), second of three. The effective map and its refusals are `quill_engine::settings` from #123; the accelerators are installed by `quill::chrome` (#119). #44 § Watch assumes an existing `notify` watcher shared with the Documents; there is none — `notify = "8"` is in the workspace and only two `//!` lines mention it — and this ticket writes it.

## What to build

A saved edit to `settings.toml` applies while Quill runs: the `[shortcuts]` table re-installs the accelerators so menu labels and the Palette show the new binding, every other setting re-applies through the same path, and a line that cannot be applied is logged once and never fatal.

Decided details:

- **Watch**: `notify-debouncer-mini` added to the workspace (`notify` 8 has no debouncer of its own), 100 ms, on the settings file's directory (editors replace the file, so watching the path alone misses the rename), in a new engine module `quill-engine/src/watch.rs` that hands the app a `std::sync::mpsc::Receiver` — the engine has no `glib`; the app drains it from a `glib` source on the main context. Written so the Documents and the Library can add paths later (the File handling spec), with a `//!` line saying so.
- **Apply**: one `Session::apply(settings)` re-applies everything the file carries — `theme` (#110), `face` and `size` (#36), `focus`, `focus_scope`, `typewriter`, `typewriter_anchor` (#114), `chrome` (#120), and now `[shortcuts]` — through the same setters the flags and the menus use. `set_accels_for_action` is called for every Command from the effective map, so a removed entry restores its default on the next apply; a chord `gtk::accelerator_parse` rejects joins the refusal list here.
- A file that fails to parse as TOML keeps the last good settings and logs the parse error once. Refusals go through `glib::g_warning!` under the domain `quill-settings`, once per distinct line per file version — a second save with the same bad line does not log again. The once-per-version rule is a pure function in the engine, tested there.
- A harness launch (any flag present) keeps overriding the file's values for that launch (`docs/architecture.md` § Command-line flags); the watch still runs so `--settings <fixture>` tests can edit the fixture.

Pieces: none.

**Size**: about 55 tool calls by the rubric — one new engine module and a dependency, one app apply path touching `session.rs`, `chrome.rs`, `editor.rs` and `window.rs` (each owns a setter), timing tests on a headless stage. The landed shape is #86 (189 calls, 228k peak); the unknown is `notify` on the headless stage.

**Reading**: #44 § Implementation Decisions (Apply, Watch, Logging) and § Testing Decisions (Headless), with the correction above. `docs/architecture.md` § Settings (the watch paragraph) and § Command-line flags. The `notify-debouncer-mini` crate docs § `new_debouncer`, not the whole crate. Skip `docs/shortcuts.md` (the rules are in the engine now) and `legacy/`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rebind `library.toggle` to `F9` in a `--settings` fixture, save; within 500 ms the effective map on the session has `F9` for it and `Ctrl+E` for nothing (the action map after the apply, without a window); `F9` reaches `win.library.toggle` in a `--deterministic` launch.
- [ ] `theme = "dark"` saved to the fixture repaints dark within 500 ms (a shot); `size = 23` re-lays the page (the same).
- [ ] Two writes 20 ms apart produce one receive (a counter on the receiver).
- [ ] A fixture with a `<Super>` chord logs one `quill-settings` warning and keeps the default; saving it again unchanged logs nothing; broken TOML keeps the last good settings and logs once — the once-per-version function tested in the engine, the domain checked in a `quill` test with a log handler.
- [ ] `tools/gate check` green.

## Blocked by

- #123
- #122

children.title: Shortcuts: the `Ctrl+?` window, the Settings window, and chrome judged with a rebinding fixture
children.body:
## Parent

Child of #44 (Shortcuts and windows), third of three and the last. The effective map is live from #124; the windows are plain GTK4 (ADR 0009); the rows the Settings window carries are the ones the port spec (#24) promised a home to; the Piece is chrome, with no new judged state, and `tools/gate judge --settings <path>` (#127) is how the judge hands the app a fixture. `GtkShortcutsWindow` is deprecated since GTK 4.18 and the workspace builds with `v4_22`, so the widget is used under `#[allow(deprecated)] // GtkShortcutsWindow: deprecated in 4.18, no replacement before GTK 5` (the one-line-reason rule in `docs/agents/gate.md`).

## What to build

The two windows: `Ctrl+?` (`shortcuts.open`) shows a `GtkShortcutsWindow` listing every Command with the chord it has right now, grouped as the menus are; `Ctrl+,` (`settings.open`) shows a small Settings window with the rows that have no menu home and a button that opens `settings.toml` in the system editor. Then `tools/gate judge chrome --settings` with a fixture that rebinds two Commands, still ours, and the Hand test comment written on #44.

Decided details:

- **Shortcuts window**: `GtkShortcutsWindow`, one section per menu (Document; View by its six subsections; Stats; Palette and keyboard only), generated from the registry's effective map on every open so an edit shows next time; Commands with no chord are listed with an empty accelerator, so the window is the whole table. The section model is a pure function of the effective map, tested in the engine.
- **Settings window**: a `GtkWindow` transient for the main window, one `GtkGrid`: Typewriter anchor (`GtkScale` 0.2–0.8 → `typewriter_anchor`), Follow System (`GtkSwitch` → `theme = "auto"`, off → the current effective scheme), Spell-check language (`GtkDropDown`, insensitive with a "Spell check: not yet built" tooltip until the Spell check spec lands), Keyboard shortcuts (`GtkButton` "Edit settings.toml…" → `gio::AppInfo::launch_default_for_uri` on the file), and, when the last apply refused a line, that line and its reason as a label at the bottom. Rows write the file through the engine and the watch (#124) applies them like any other edit — no direct setter call.
- Both are actions from the registry (#119); their chords are in `docs/shortcuts.md` already.
- Judge: `tools/gate judge chrome --settings quill/tests/fixtures/rebind.toml`, the fixture rebinding `library.toggle` and `theme.toggle`; all four states still ours (labels change, layout does not).
- This ticket writes the Hand test comment on #44 (its six steps from § Further Notes and the install commands, in full); the spec closes on the owner's `hand test: pass`, not on this ticket.

Pieces: chrome.

**Size**: about 50 tool calls by the rubric — two windows from stock widgets, one fixture, one judge run; budget for two rounds. The landed shape is #102 (127 calls, 169k peak).

**Reading**: #44 § Implementation Decisions (Shortcuts window, Settings window) and § Further Notes (the Hand test steps, which name what each row does). ADR 0009. `docs/agents/gate.md` § Ticket tier, Blind judging. GTK4's `GtkShortcutsWindow` docs § the section/group/shortcut model. Skip `legacy/` whole; the oracle has neither window.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The shortcuts model for the rebinding fixture lists `F9` for `library.toggle` and every other Command with its default or nothing (engine test); `Ctrl+?` shows it (a shot).
- [ ] Moving the anchor scale writes `typewriter_anchor` to the fixture file; Follow System writes `theme = "auto"` (the file's contents after the write).
- [ ] "Edit settings.toml…" launches the default handler for the file's URI (the launch call's arguments, through a stub).
- [ ] A refused line from the last apply is shown in the Settings window; none shown when there is none (the label's model, not the widget).
- [ ] `tools/gate judge chrome --settings` with the rebinding fixture: all four states ours, round committed; the Hand test comment is on #44; `tools/gate check` green.

## Blocked by

- #124
